subject: Pinebrook: AZ1 sustained 5xx & latency spike — urgent cross-region rehome request
messages:
From: Michael Liu <michael.liu@pinebrook.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-01T08:04:03-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook: sudden latency and 500s since 07:45 PT

Grace / Marissa —

We started seeing a sharp P95 latency increase and 5xx rates climbing in us-west-2 AZ1 around 07:45 PT. Our telemetry shows P95 went from ~420ms to 3.2s and 5xx rates averaging 6.7% across the customer-facing endpoints. Error responses are predominantly 502/504 originating in your inference tier — traces show KV cache timeouts and worker queue saturations.

This is customer-impacting — users on our west coast fleet are seeing timeouts and a large drop in throughput. Can Redwood initiate an immediate cross-region rehome to eastus2 (we will accept traffic routed to eastus2 for the next 2–3 hours) while you stabilize AZ1? We also need an exported set of the last hour of KV cache and request traces.

I can approve the temporary routing change from our side, but would like confirmation on rollback criteria and estimated timing for the canary. Also, please flag if any config changes will impact data residency — we are on a contract with specific region clauses.

Thanks —
Michael
Ops Lead, Pinebrook Systems
attachments: kvcache-metrics-2027-05-01.csv

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Liu <michael.liu@pinebrook.io>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:12:18-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook: AZ1 sustained 5xx & latency spike — urgent cross-region rehome request

Looping in infra and routing ops. Rishi — can you confirm current root cause hypothesis and whether we can do a safe canary to eastus2? Vanessa / Marissa — please note exec attention and potential credit ask.

Initial ask:
- Can we push a 5% canary to eastus2 within 10 minutes, expand to 25%/50% over 20 minutes if metrics look healthy?
- Do we need a model-variant fallback or will routing alone be sufficient?
- Share rollback criteria (error rate, P95 threshold).
- Provide the KV cache traces Michael requested (attach).

I will update Pinebrook that we have a canary plan and expected timeline once we have confirmation. If this looks like a regional capacity or kernel-level regression we should escalate immediately to Exec pager (Marissa please advise).

—Grace
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Liu <michael.liu@pinebrook.io>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:22:34-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook: AZ1 sustained 5xx & latency spike — urgent cross-region rehome request

Quick triage notes (observed at 08:20 PT):
- Root cause candidate: KVCACHE eviction/thrashing under a burst of large-batch prefix requests — we see a sharp KVS latency tail and persistent lock contention on shard-07.
- Queue depth on the inference workers in AZ1 hit 6x normal for ~6m starting 07:46. Backpressure then cascaded into upstream timeouts and proxy 502/504.
- No config changes rolled out in the last 24h; kernels and quantization profiles unchanged.

Operational plan (recommended):
1) Begin a traffic canary: route 5% of Pinebrook traffic from us-west-2/az1 -> eastus2. Monitor P95 and 5xx for 5 minutes.
2) If P95 < 700ms and 5xx < 1% -> advance to 25% over next 10 minutes.
3) If at any step 5xx > 2% or P95 > 1.5s rollback to AZ1 routing.
4) In parallel, trigger a per-prefix KV cache warmup on eastus2 to avoid cold miss amplification (script queued).

I attached the last-hour KVCACHE snapshot and a quick heatmap. If eastus2 shows similar eviction patterns we will need to spin up an extra worker pool or activate the fallback model variant (lower memory footprint) — that would add latency regressions but reduce 5xx risk.

I will start the canary when I get explicit approval from Pinebrook (Michael) and go/no-go from Vanessa on any contractual region constraints.

-Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: kvcache-metrics-2027-05-01.csv; network-map-az1-eastus2.png

From: Michael Liu <michael.liu@pinebrook.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T08:35:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook: AZ1 sustained 5xx & latency spike — urgent cross-region rehome request

Thanks Rishi — Pinebrook approves the proposed canary. We understand the rollback triggers. Confirming we accept traffic in eastus2 for the next 3 hours.

Two asks from our side:
- Please add a temporary rate limit (server-side) on the /v1/batch and /v1/interactive endpoints to blunt the worst-requestors while you expand canary. We will also throttle from our client side but would prefer server-side protection.
- We will log a billing dispute if API errors exceed 3% for more than 30m — Marissa / Grace, please advise on credit policy.

Michael
Ops Lead, Pinebrook Systems

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Liu <michael.liu@pinebrook.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:40-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinebrook: AZ1 sustained 5xx & latency spike — urgent cross-region rehome request

Update for execs and Pinebrook:
- Rishi started the 5% canary at 08:44 PT. Initial 5-minute check: P95 eastus2 = 560ms, 5xx = 0.6%. Advancing to 25% at 08:50.
- At 08:58 we reached 25% with P95 = 620ms and 5xx = 0.9%. Proceeding to 50% hold.
- Temporary server-side rate limits applied to /v1/batch and /v1/interactive (throttle to 120 RPS per shard for Pinebrook).
- Pinebrook confirmed acceptance of eastus2 routing. They flagged potential credit ask if errors exceed 3% for 30m — Marissa please capture for CS/Finance review.

Next steps: continue to monitor for 1h. If AZ1 stabilizes (P95 < 700ms and 5xx < 1%) we will perform a controlled drain back to AZ1; otherwise keep traffic in eastus2 and provision additional worker capacity as needed.

I have flagged this for Marissa and Vanessa for any exec-level customer outreach and credit decisions.

—Grace
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
